A Buddhist teacher from Bengal, born in 982, who became one of the main founders of the second spread of Buddhism in Tibet. He died there in 1054.

Born a prince, he took monastic vows and studied widely. Tradition says he sailed to Suvarnadvipa, in the Srivijaya realm of Sumatra, and studied for twelve years under a master there. Back in India he became a leading scholar at the monastery of Vikramashila, founded by the Pala kings.

Tibet's Buddhist institutions had broken down after the fall of the Tibetan Empire. The rulers of Guge in western Tibet invited him, and after long persuasion he set out in 1040. He spent his last years teaching in Tibet. His short text A Lamp for the Path to Enlightenment lays out graded stages of practice for all kinds of students.

His disciple Dromtonpa founded the Kadam school, whose ideas later fed the Gelug school of Tsongkhapa. See also Atisha comes to Tibet.
sum: A Buddhist teacher from Bengal, born in 982, who became one of the main founders of the second spread of Buddhism in Tibet. He died there in 1054.
